result.topic_en: Finite closed forms, valid when 2α (or α) is a positive integer, for series of the type Σ n/(n^4+4α^4), together with a related integral and a residue-theory identity involving coth, from which a series with weights 1/(e^{2πn}-1) is evaluated.
result.transcription:
Add. Ms a 94 $^{18(59)}$ (59) (4)
5. If $2\alpha$ be a positive integer, then it can easily be shown that
(13) $\frac{1}{1^4+4\alpha^4}+\frac{2}{2^4+4\alpha^4}+\frac{3}{3^4+4\alpha^4}+\cdots\cdots$
$=\frac{1}{4\alpha}\left\{\frac{1}{(1-\alpha)^2+\alpha^2}+\frac{1}{(2-\alpha)^2+\alpha^2}+\frac{1}{(3-\alpha)^2+\alpha^2}+\cdots\text{ to }2\alpha\text{ terms}\right\}$;
and
(14) $\int_0^\infty\frac{x}{e^{2\pi x}-1}\cdot\frac{dx}{4\alpha^4+x^4}=\frac{\pi}{8\alpha^2}\frac{(-1)^{2\alpha}}{e^{2\pi\alpha}+(-1)^{2\alpha+1}}$
$+\frac{1}{8\alpha}\left\{\frac{1}{(1-\alpha)^2+\alpha^2}+\frac{1}{(2-\alpha)^2+\alpha^2}+\frac{1}{(3-\alpha)^2+\alpha^2}+\cdots\text{to }2\alpha\text{ terms}\right\}$
It can easily be shown by the theory of residues, that
(15) $\frac{1}{16\pi\alpha^4}+\frac{\coth\pi}{1^4+4\alpha^4}+\frac{2\coth 2\pi}{2^4+4\alpha^4}+\frac{3\coth 3\pi}{3^4+4\alpha^4}+\cdots$
$=\frac{\pi}{8\alpha^2}\cdot\frac{\cosh 2\pi\alpha+\cos 2\pi\alpha}{\cosh 2\pi\alpha-\cos 2\pi\alpha}$.
It follows from (13) and (15) that, if $2\alpha$ be a positive integer, then
(16) $\frac{1}{e^{2\pi}-1}\cdot\frac{1}{1^4+4\alpha^4}+\frac{2}{e^{4\pi}-1}\cdot\frac{1}{2^4+4\alpha^4}+\frac{3}{e^{6\pi}-1}\cdot\frac{1}{3^4+4\alpha^4}+\cdots$
$=\frac{\pi}{16\alpha^2}\cdot\left\{\frac{e^{2\pi\alpha}+(-1)^{2\alpha}}{e^{2\pi\alpha}-(-1)^{2\alpha}}\right\}^2-\frac{1}{32\pi\alpha^4}$
$-\frac{1}{8\alpha}\left\{\frac{1}{(1-\alpha)^2+\alpha^2}+\frac{1}{(2-\alpha)^2+\alpha^2}+\cdots\text{ to }2\alpha\text{ terms}\right\}$
In a similar manner we can show that, if $\alpha$ be a positive integer then
(17) $\frac{1}{1^4+4\alpha^4}+\frac{3}{3^4+4\alpha^4}+\frac{5}{5^4+4\alpha^4}+\cdots$
$=\frac{1}{4\alpha}\left\{\frac{1}{(1-\alpha)^2+\alpha^2}+\frac{1}{(3-\alpha)^2+\alpha^2}+\frac{1}{(5-\alpha)^2+\alpha^2}+\cdots\text{to }\alpha\text{ terms}\right\}$;
